morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with habitat and growth form: a rhizomatous aquatic perennial forming colonies in shallow moving water, with long narrow opposite leaves and long-peduncled axillary flower spikes.
diagnostic_traits: erect shoots from shoreline or shallow water
white flowers with purple spotting on the lower lip

confusers.separator: Water-willow is a tall glabrous aquatic colony-former with long narrow leaves; J. pilosella is a tiny dry-site hairy mound.

taxonomy.notes: Current POWO accepts Dianthera americana; Texas and many U.S. field sources still commonly use Justicia americana. Preserve Justicia americana as a prominent alias/search term.

evidence_basis: Hays — UT Purola Preserve natural flora records Justicia americana.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Acanthaceae index documents Justicia americana.
Williamson — UT Vascular Plants of Williamson County includes Justicia americana.
POWO confirms Texas is within the native range of accepted Dianthera americana.

morphology.look_here_first: Aquatic/riparian colony-forming habit, long narrow opposite leaves, and peduncled axillary flower spikes.
morphology.key_separator: Distinct from Justicia pilosella by its tall glabrous rhizomatous water-edge habit and much longer narrow leaves.
